findings.title: Team admin check uses AND of isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. The name and intent call for OR. With AND, only users who are both admin and owner pass, so team admins who are not owners are wrongly denied. Fix by using `||`. Also, for bookings with no team, `teamId ?? 0` queries team id 0, which is pointless.

findings.title: Any attendee can add guests to a booking
findings.body: Authorization allows any existing attendee, matched by `attendee.email === user.email`. This lets a guest add arbitrary new attendees to someone else's booking. Each new attendee triggers confirmation emails sent from the organizer's identity, and the guests are added to the organizer's calendar event, which is a spam and abuse vector. The email match is also not restricted to a verified or case-normalized email. Restrict to the organizer and team admins/owners, or at least tighten the check.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased, but `guest` is compared as-is. `Blocked@x.com` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. The same applies to the dedup check against existing attendees (`guest === attendee.email`), so differently-cased duplicates can be added. Also, duplicates within the input list itself are not removed server-side (the client check is bypassable), so `createMany` can insert duplicate attendees. Normalize case and dedupe on the server.

findings.title: Emails use the raw input `guests` list instead of the filtered unique guests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original input, not `uniqueGuests`. Guests that were filtered out as already-attending or blacklisted are treated as new, so existing attendees get a full 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notification. A guest the server rejected can also get the new-guest email. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the acting user's credentials and identity, not the organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({...user, credentials})` use the logged-in user. If an attendee or team admin triggers this, the booking's calendar event (owned by the organizer's credentials) cannot be updated correctly, or the update silently fails. The handler also loads `booking.user.credentials` but never uses it. The `updateCalendarAttendees` call is not wrapped in try/catch either. A calendar failure after the DB write has committed leaves the attendees saved but the request failing, and no emails are sent.

findings.title: New guests are created with an empty name and the organizer's locale/timezone
findings.body: Guests are created with `name: ""`, and `timeZone` and `locale` copied from the organizer. The guest's email therefore renders with no name, and the email language and time zone are the organizer's, not the guest's. For organizer emails, `attendees[0].name` is used in the subject, which stays correct only while the first attendee is the original booker. Also, the `catch` at the end logs a static message and discards the error.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email-disable settings and sends full scheduled email to new guests
findings.body: Unlike the other send functions, it takes no `eventTypeMetadata` and never checks `disableStandardEmails` for host or attendee, so emails get sent even when the event type has disabled them. When `calendarEvent.team` is set, the organizer email is sent once without a teamMember and then once per team member. The sequence matches the existing patterns, but the guard checks are missing.

findings.title: Add guests action is offered for all editable bookings, including seated and past bookings
findings.body: The 'add_members' action is added unconditionally to `editBookingActions`. It also appears on past confirmed/pending bookings and on seated events. For seated events, attendees are individual seats and adding guests this way breaks seat accounting (`seatsPerTimeSlot`). There is no gating on seats or on the booking being upcoming.

findings.title: Error message formatting is wrong and the fallback is unreachable
findings.body: `message` is always a non-empty template string like `BAD_REQUEST: ...`, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never applies. The code prefix is also exposed to users. `isInvalidEmail` is never reset to false after the user edits the field or after a successful add, so the error banner persists. Empty strings in the input array (the initial `[""]`) fail the email validation, but only the generic 'unique and valid' message is shown.

findings.title: Hard-coded English tooltip and index-based React keys
findings.body: The tooltip `"Remove email"` is not translated. The list uses `key={index}`, so removing a middle entry in a controlled list of inputs can misattribute input state. The `label htmlFor="emails"` points to no element id.
